messages:
jess: Heads-up — last night we got a bunch of DCGM Exporter alerts in eu-west for Xid/ ECC spikes on a few nodes. Looks like noisy one-offs rather than clear card failures. Posting samples and a quick hypothesis.
kyle: saw ~6 alerts between 02:15–02:40 UTC on 3 nodes. All different cards, same rack. Node-level health was fine, tests passed. No immediate regressions in job throughput.
lia: do you have the raw metric windows? might be sample-rate related (collector burst) or a prometheus rule that's too sensitive on single-sample blips.
jess: pasted the scrapes and a candidate rule we used to alert — current prom rule triggers if dcgm_gpu_ecc_xid_events_total increases by >0 in 1m per card. That feels noisy.
jess: ```
# current noisy rule
expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_xid_events_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[1m]) > 0
for: 0m
labels:
  severity: critical
``` 
ana: ouch — 1m with no for= looks primed for flapping. Also DCGM can emit transient spikes during MIG moves, driver rebinds, or nvlink retries. We should correlate with node-level events.
ron: i pulled node events: kernel logs show a quick pci reset on one node at 02:18, and a k8s pod eviction on another at 02:20. So not all spikes are true card defects.
kyle: proposal: change to a small scoring window + require persistent signal across multiple windows. e.g., sum over 5m of increases and require >=3 distinct 1m windows with >0 events, or use percentile to ignore single extreme short spikes.
lia: propose new rule POC:
```yaml
expr: (
  sum by(gpu_uuid)(increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_xid_events_total[1m]) > 0)
)
  and on(gpu_uuid)
(
  count_over_time((increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_xid_events_total[1m]) > 0)[10m:1m]) >= 3
)
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
``` 
jess: that looks promising. The count_over_time trick avoids firing on single blips. We should also reduce cardinality explosion — group by node and gpu_index not full job labels.
ana: also add a suppression rule if node has been recently drained or rebooted: label nodes with node_maintenance=true, and silence alerts for 15m after drain event. Ops-bot can stamp that.
ops-bot: ack — can emit node_maintenance=true when a drain job/annotation detected. I'll add an event marker we can join on via metrics.
ron: one more gotcha: exporter scrape jitter. If scrape sometimes stalls, increase() windows can appear larger. We should ensure scrape interval and prometheus retention match our rule windows.
kyle: action items:
- kyle: implement POC rule in staging (prometheus-staging) — change sample window to 1m slices with count_over_time 10m, require >=3 — test for 48h
- jess: correlate the 3 noisy nodes with PCI events and MIG reassignments
- lia: add a recording rule that computes per-card "transient_score" so dashboards use smoothed numbers
- ron: add a silence hook to ops-bot when node drains are initiated
ana: i'll open the PR for the prom rule POC and include example graphs (before/after) and a brief test run log. tag:eng-oncall for visibility.
jess: thanks — let's avoid auto-draining cards unless the rule is satisfied for >=30m and we see repeated ECC/Xid and NVML errors. For now just better alert discrimination.
kyle: noted. i'll post the staging link once rule is live.
lia: :thumbsup: good compromise — reduces false positives and keeps ops escalation strict.
ops-bot: created issue INFRA-2342 and attached initial silence API doc snippet. Link: https://ourjira/INFRA-2342
jess: great. i'll follow up in the morning with correlation artifacts and a short runbook tweak.
